description.value: A resting-state fMRI study comparing ventral and dorsal striatum functional connectivity between excess-weight and normal-weight participants and examining associations with food craving, compulsivity, and BMI change.

spans.text: We aimed to contrast the functional connectivity of ventral and dorsal striatum networks in excess-weight versus normal-weight participants and to determine the association between functional connectivity in the striatum and individual differences in food craving and weight gain.

value: We hypothesized that excess-weight participants compared with normal-weight control subjects would show increased functional connectivity in the ventral and dorsal striatum.
Increased dorsal striatal connectivity would be associated with greater food craving and weight gain.

spans.text: We hypothesized that excess-weight participants compared with normal-weight control subjects would show increased functional connectivity in the ventral and dorsal striatum. Increased dorsal striatal connectivity would be associated with greater food craving and weight gain.

description.value: Observational study with baseline resting-state fMRI and food-craving assessment, followed by a 12-week BMI follow-up in the excess-weight group.

value: In excess-weight participants, food craving was positively associated with functional connectivity between the DC seed and the somatosensory cortex.
The dorsal caudate-somatosensory cortex association with food craving accords with previous studies showing increased dorsal caudate activation in response to palatable food cues in obesity.
The link between the dorsal striatum network and food craving was significant in the excess-weight group and greater within participants with higher BMI values.
